transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-01-22
Start: 15:30 UTC
Duration: 62 minutes
Attendees: Alyssa Chen (Redwood AE), Devon Park (Redwood SE), Samir Rao (Redwood Solutions), Maya Singh (CyberGuard Head of Security), Raj Patel (Cloud Architect), Lena Ortiz (Vendor Risk), Tom Baker (Compliance)
Shared links: https://redwood.example.com/security/soc2-redacted.pdf (placeholder), Drive: /CyberGuard/SIG-template-v2.xlsx

Summary:
Quick SIG/CAIQ walkthrough and evidence mapping. Customer clarified scope: EU data residency for production, want SOC 2 Type II + ISO artifacts, customer-managed KMS for keys in Private/Dedicated, RBAC & SSO via Okta, audit log retention 18 months minimum, and requirement to show access logs for privileged actions. Action items and a follow-up on KMS integration were agreed.

Topics: SOC 2 evidences, ISO certs, SIG spreadsheet walkthrough, CAIQ partials, RBAC/SSO mapping, audit logs schema, KMS + BYOK, data residency constraints, evidence packaging timeline.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Alyssa: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intro — I'm Alyssa, I'll own the security thread on this deal. Devon from our SE team, Samir's sat in for solutions and evidence packaging.
[00:15] Maya: Hi, thanks. We'll do a short context set — CyberGuard's procurement needs the SIG completed and we want to map to our vendor risk controls. We're particularly focused on data residency and key management.
[00:30] Raj: Yes, production must live in eu-west-1 and logs cannot leave region. We also need to see how Redwood handles customer-managed keys; we have an internal KMS policy for bring-your-own-key.
[00:45] Devon: Got it. To set expectations, Redwood has three deployment modes — hosted, dedicated, and private; the private deployment supports customer KMS and isolated control plane; dedicated can offer strong isolation but keys are managed differently depending on the plan.
[01:05] Lena: Can you clarify the difference — we need to know if we can rotate keys from our side and whether the vendor can access plaintext at any stage.
[01:18] Devon: Sure. In Private we support BYOK backed by AWS KMS — the key policy and encryption happen in your account; Redwood only gets ciphertext. For Dedicated there's a customer KMS integration option but it depends on contract and network topology. We'll pull the exact KMS flow diagram into the folder.
[01:42] Tom: Ok, what about audit logs? We need to capture admin actions, model rollouts, and API key usage. Retention is 18 months minimal for us.
[01:55] Samir: We emit audit events for admin console, model deploys, and token issuance. Standard retention on hosted is 12 months, but Dedicated/Private you can configure longer retention or forward to customer SIEM (we support S3 export and CloudWatch/Events forwarding).
[02:18] Maya: That aligns, but we need an example of the audit schema — fields and sample log lines.
[02:30] Devon: I'll attach an example export (json lines) — it includes timestamp, principal, action, resource, request id, and optional model metadata. I'll mark which fields are retained for 18 months.
[02:48] [Speaker 1]: (inaudible) question on SOC 2 — do you have the most recent report?
[02:55] Alyssa: Yes, we'll share a redacted SOC 2 Type II PDF — control narratives and the opinion page. We won't share raw evidence but can supply evidence mapping for the SIG answers referencing test IDs from the report.
[03:15] Raj: For the SIG, we need explicit evidence file names and locations for each answered question — a lot of vendors put "see SOC 2" without mapping. Can you do a mapping sheet?
[03:30] Alyssa: Absolutely, Samir will produce a mapping tab: SIG question -> answer -> evidence doc (SOC2 page x, pen test report section y, config checklist z).
[03:42] Maya: And CAIQ? We typically accept CAIQ partials plus SIG.
[03:48] Devon: We'll populate CAIQ responses for the control categories we cover. For items we don't support we'll mark with a caveat and suggested compensating control.
[04:05] Lena: About SSO and RBAC — we use Okta as IdP with SCIM for provisioning. Can Redwood integrate with SCIM?
[04:18] Devon: Yes, Redwood supports SAML SSO and SCIM for user provisioning. RBAC uses roles (admin/operator/audit) — roles can be mapped to Okta groups. We can provide the SAML metadata and SCIM schema in the shared folder.
[04:38] Maya: Fine. We also need to know how API keys are scoped and whether service accounts can be locked to IPs.
[04:48] Dev(on): API keys are tokenized, can be scoped by model and route. IP allowlist is supported on Dedicated and Private and on hosted via per-account allowlist policies. We'll include the API key policy doc.
[05:10] Raj: What's the expected lead time for Private deployment? We may need air-gapped options for certain environments.
[05:20] Alyssa: Private on-prem or VPC options typically run a 6–10 week onboarding depending on network approvals and access. Air-gapped has extra steps for packaging. We'll add the onboarding checklist.
[05:37] Tom: SOC 2 — do you have ISO 27001 as well? Our procurement likes both.
[05:44] Alyssa: We have ISO 27001 certification; we'll share cert and scope document.
[05:50] [00:06:00] Maya: Great. Regarding pen tests, do you do annual 3rd party penetration tests?
[06:08] Samir: Yes, annual third-party pen tests; we can share executive summary and remediation timeline. We won't share vulnerability detail publically but we can provide redacted scan results and POA&Ms where appropriate.
[06:24] Raj: For CAIQ question CAI-010 about key lifecycle, can you provide the rotation cadence and method?
[06:33] Devon: Rotation depends on KMS policy; for customer-managed keys rotation is under your control. For vendor-managed keys we enforce a rotation policy and can provide attestation for the rotation events.
[06:48] [00:07:00] Lena: On encryption at rest — algorithm and cipher suites? We need AES-256 and TLS 1.2+ for in transit.
[07:10] Devon: Yes, AES-256 for at-rest and TLS 1.2 or 1.3 for in-transit. We'll include the crypto spec sheet.
[07:25] Maya: Data residency in EU — can you guarantee logs never leave eu-west-1 even for analysis?
[07:36] Devon: For Private deployments we can lock logs to the region. For hosted we currently route EU data to eu-west-1, but backups and certain telemetry can be replicated to other regions for reliability; we can provide controls and contractual terms to restrict replication. We'll mark that as a legal requirement to discuss.
[07:58] Raj: Ok, we need a definitive statement for the SIG: where is data processed and stored by component?
[08:09] Alyssa: We'll produce a component map: control plane location, data plane location, model storage, embeddings store, and logging endpoints. It will be in the shared DRIVE folder.
[08:25] [00:09:00] Tom: Regarding access reviews and privileged access — do you support periodic attestation?
[08:34] Samir: Yes, we have audit trails and can export access review reports. We also support role-based approvals and integration with Okta for SAML + enforced MFA.
[08:48] Maya: Any limitations for HIPAA workloads?
[08:55] Devon: We support HIPAA when on Dedicated/Private with BAAs in place. Hosted is more limited; we'd review with legal.
[09:10] Raj: On CFR/PCI: any specific modules not allowed?
[09:16] Alyssa: We don't position for direct PCI processing of cardholder data in the hosted environment unless architected into a private topology; we can detail the boundaries in the architecture doc.
[09:30] [00:10:00] Lena: Back to evidence requests — can you provide an index of artifacts (naming convention + redacted sample) so our team can map quickly?
[09:40] Samir: Yes — index will include file name, control mapped, redaction level, and contact for follow-up. We'll populate the SIG spreadsheet column with that info.
[09:52] Raj: We also want to see a sample of your penetration testing provider's scope and methodology.
[09:58] Samir: We'll include the pen-test scope and the high-level methodology in the shared folder; vendor names might be redacted for confidentiality but we can provide accreditation.
[10:12] Maya: One of our security controls asks for "evidence of management of secrets" — how do you handle secrets for model weights and config?
[10:23] Devon: Secrets (like API keys, DB credentials) are stored in customer KMS or in a secrets manager for Dedicated/Private; for hosted we use a vault with encryption at rest and strict access controls. We'll map this to SIG controls and provide a flow diagram.
[10:40] [00:11:00] Tom: Regarding vulnerability disclosure and bug bounty — do you have a program?
[10:48] Alyssa: We have a coordinated vulnerability disclosure policy and a limited bug bounty program for critical components; we'll share the policy link and response SLAs.
[11:00] Raj: How do you handle data subject requests (DSRs) for GDPR?
[11:08] Devon: We have tooling to find and remove user-level data on request for customers on Private/Dedicated, and for hosted we provide an API and support to assist with exports and deletions. We can provide playbooks.
[11:25] Maya: Great. Anything else around SLA and incident response?
[11:32] Alyssa: We'll attach our incident response playbook (redacted) and the SLA doc. For Dedicated customers we have 24/7 support options.
[11:45] [00:12:00] Lena: For the SIG question on background checks for personnel, do you have a standard?
[11:51] Samir: Yes — background checks for employees in sensitive roles; we'll provide the HR policy extract.
[12:00] Raj: Is there any PCI-like segmentation for embeddings store? We don't want PII to be mixed with model-indexed data.
[12:11] Devon: Embeddings are treated as model artifacts and can be isolated by tenant; you can configure separate stores for sensitive namespaces on Private/Dedicated.
[12:25] Maya: Ok, can we talk about timeline — we need SIG completed within two weeks for procurement gating.
[12:33] Alyssa: Two weeks is tight but doable if we align: we'll push the SOC2 redacted and mapping by next Wednesday and ask you to complete the SIG spreadsheet with any follow-ups.
[12:45] Lena: Will you be able to sign a data processing addendum with EU-specific clauses?
[12:51] Alyssa: Yes, DPA with EU addendum is standard; we'll attach the template.
[12:59] [00:13:00] Raj: One technical question — KV cache and prefix caching: do you store prefixes in plaintext anywhere? We need to ensure no PII is stored without consent.
[13:12] Devon: Caches are ephemeral and encrypted; for hosted we have TTLs and options to disable prefix caching. We'll note where caching occurs in the architecture doc.
[13:28] Tom: Thanks. For the next steps on our side — we'll compile the SIG and flag the highest risk items for follow-up.
[13:36] Maya: Can we get a short call focusing on KMS next week? Raj and I will attend.
[13:42] Alyssa: Yes — Devon will set up a KMS deep dive; I'll send a calendar invite after the call.
[13:50] 
[00:50:00] (Wrap-up)
[50:10] Alyssa: Quick recap — action items: Redwood to share SOC2 redacted, ISO cert, pen test summary, audit log schema, and KMS diagram. Customer to fill SIG template and confirm EU residency specifics. We'll target follow-up KMS deep dive on Wednesday next week.
[50:35] Maya: Sounds good. Thank you all.
[50:38] Raj: Thanks, talk soon.
[50:40] Devon: Thanks everyone.

End of transcript.

Notes on transcription quality: occasional overlaps and some words were unclear (e.g., speaker labeled as Speaker 1 at 02:48). The timestamps are approximate and inserted every 15–90 seconds to mirror Fireflies export behavior.
